title: Signature, Activation and Lapse of a Patient Payment Plan Agreement
content:
**Patient Financial Services policy — the signed Patient Payment Plan agreement**

(a) A Patient Payment Plan agreement becomes binding only when the patient signs it; the clinic never signs on the patient's behalf.

(b) On signing, every enrolled charge moves into the plan and is removed from its plan of care as a transfer to the payment plan, and any down payment is taken. The agreement moves from pending signature to active.

(c) An agreement still unsigned lapses no earlier than the tier's signature window, in calendar days, after the enrollment date on file. Days are counted as calendar days from the enrollment date, the enrollment date itself being day zero.

(d) A lapsed agreement leaves the charges on their plans of care. The agreement closes as cancelled for not being signed.

## The lapse clock in brief

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| Event the clock starts from | The enrollment date recorded on that agreement |
| Day zero | The enrollment date itself |
| Unit | Calendar days |
| Earliest lapse | The day on which the count reaches the tier's signature window; that day itself is included |
| Before that day | The unsigned agreement does not lapse |

## Timeline (hypothetical dates, signature window of 7 days)

- Enrollment date 2026-02-03 is day 0.
- 2026-02-09 is day 6: the unsigned agreement does not yet lapse.
- 2026-02-10 is day 7: the earliest day on which the unsigned agreement may lapse.

If the patient signs while the agreement is still pending signature, clause (b) applies: the charges move into the plan and any down payment is taken. If it lapses, clause (d) applies: the charges stay on their plans of care.
